Sam — thanks for the brief and the requirements doc. High level recommendation below; I’ll follow up with a concise spreadsheet (BR_quote_20260704.xlsx) before our call.

Recommendation (short):
- Pilot: 3-month pilot on Compact with the following add-ons enabled: prefix caching, re-ranking, and audit-log retention (90 days). This minimizes upfront cost while validating traffic patterns.
- Production: move to Core Plus (metered tokens + feature bundle) if latency at pilot volumes is within SLOs; if predicted 95th p99 latency targets need dedicated GPUs, we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) and we’ll model cost vs throughput.

Rationale: Compact + add-ons gets you most features at lowest cost; Core Plus buys better tail latency and higher concurrency. Dedicated only if expected sustained throughput exceeds our burst windows or if Brightline requires tenant isolation for compliance.

Pricing / discounts / downgrade guardrails:
- We can offer a pilot concession: 50% off token usage for the first month, 25% off for months 2–3 with a short-term SOW.
- For a 12-month commit we can do a 15% list discount on the quoted bundle and waive the SSO onboarding fee.
- For a 6-month commit we can do a 10% discount.
- Downgrades: we offer a 60-day grace window after production go-live where you can step down one tier and receive prorated credits applied to the next invoice (credits = remaining committed value * pro-rata factor less implementation cost). We document the exact proration formula in the quote.

Operational notes / tradeoffs:
- Feature bundling: re-ranking + audit logs + prefix cache can be toggled without rolling models, but disabled features may leave cached KV state that requires a short warm-up on flip.
- Quantization/throughput: if you accept int8 quantized variants we can reduce reserved capacity cost by roughly 20% at slightly higher latency variance.

Next steps:
1) I’ll send BR_quote_20260704.xlsx with line-item pricing and the formal proration math.
2) Let’s book a 30-min sync (I’m available Tue/Wed mornings).
3) If procurement needs specific language on downgrade credits, loop legal and we’ll insert a short amendment.

Looping Marissa (CS lead) to confirm support SLA and onboarding timelines.

Best,

Sam — appreciate the transparency on targets. Quick counter-proposal to drive to signature while protecting both sides: 

Commercials:
- 12-month commit: 18% off quoted bundle (list) + waived SSO onboarding fee + 6 months of extended audit-log retention included.
- 6-month commit: 12% off quoted bundle + waived SSO onboarding fee.
- Pilot: a hybrid pilot — month 1 at 100% discount on platform fees (we’ll cover base platform for month 1), months 2–3 at 40% discount. Pilot success metric is latency & token spend thresholds; if you exceed the thresholds we’ll accelerate to a production proposal.

Downgrade / proration mechanics (example):
- Example quote: 12-mo commit for $120k (committed spend). If you step down at month 4 with 8 months remaining, the remaining committed value is $80k. We apply a pro-rata adjustment (we cap implementation offset at $10k) and issue a credit for ($80k - $10k) * 0.75 = $52.5k applied over next two invoices. Exact formula will be in the SOW.

Concessions we can add if you need more headroom:
- Extended support (24x5) for first 6 months at no additional charge.
- A one-time onboarding credit to offset pilot ramp.

If Brightline can accept 18% on 12 months I can approve it via my quota authority; I’d ask procurement to confirm the internal timeline and we’ll put a clean DocuSign to route (link included). If they still push to 25% we can explore a one-time performance credit structure instead of list discount.

Proposed next step: Lauren will send the numeric quote with the proration table and a DocuSign wrapper by EOD Friday. If you want to take the 18% we’ll prepare a redline-friendly SOW.

Thanks —
